To begin treatment, take the goat to a far away place away from grazing lands and sheds. Preferably, this place should be isolated and is in a part of the farm that is not visited by animals or humans.
Treat all lumps on the goat's body at the same time to not risk spreading the disease.
Make sure that all who are involved in treating the goat now are wearing gloves!
Cut open the lump(s) carefully with a blade or a scalpel around its rim where it meets the goat's body.
Drain the pus inside carefully initially with the help of the blade or scalpel. Take extra precautions to make sure your clothing or shoes is not contaminated by the pus!
After the pus has been removed completely, flush the wound and its surroundings with oxytetracycline 50mg thouroughly to cover all parts of the wound.
Now flush the wound and its surroundings with iodine thoroughly.
After making sure that all of the pus has been removed, spray aluspray over the wound so as to cover it and let it heal. Do not cover it with a bandage or cloth!
Shift the animal to a quarantine partition that has no animals or only has animals treated for lumps.
Spray aluspray everyday.

Unfortunately, there exist no proper treatments specifically for body edema as the cause is still unknown.
If it presents itself as a symptom of some disease that has been diagnosed, then follow that disease’s SOP.
Just make sure that the animal is hydrated and eating. If not eating, follow the Not eating SOP.
Take two straight firm sticks.

If the fracture is below the knee, cut the sticks to be long enough to span the knee from the ankle. If the fracture is above the knee, cut the sticks to be long enough to span the shoulder from the knee.
Wrap the sticks in a cloth firmly. Use tape if needed to hold the cloth in place.
Place the sticks from the knee towards the direction of the fracture, opposite to each other. The sticks should sandwich the fractured bone.
Wrap this sandwich tightly with crepe bandage. Use crepe bandage profusely so that it hold the bone and sticks in place and tie it tightly at the end.

Wrap this sandwich tightly with crepe bandage. Use crepe bandage profusely so that it hold the bone and sticks in place and tie it tightly at the end.
